text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas will submit to parliament Homeland Union chairman Gediminas Vagnorius as the only candidate to the post of new prime minister, most probably on Wednesday. The new cabinet is expected to be formed within two weeks.

- Brazauskas confirmed he will visit Riga and attend the summit of the three Baltic presidents on Tuesday despite the reported insults to Lithuanian officials by Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele in a Lithuanian newspaper.
- The leadership of former ruling party the Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party (LDLP) might resign during an LDLP council meeting on Saturday.
- Russian gas concern Gazprom has threatened once again to cut natural gas supplies to Lithuania from December 1 if a $30.8 million debt is not paid.

- Ignalina nuclear power plant is as safe as the majority of nuclear power plants in the West and there is no need to close it early. If the fuel is changed it might even operate longer than 2010, said the company director Victor Shevaldin.
- The biggest private financial institution in Lithuania Vilnius Bank reported a 16 million litas profit for the nine months of the year.
- On October 1, seven out of 12 commercial banks were meeting all the required standards on risk limits, the central bank, the Bank of Lithuania, said.
- The Bank of Lithuania decided to initiate a bankruptcy case against the insolvent Senamiescio Bank.

- Three statues of St Stanislovas, St Kazimieras and St Elena will be re-erected Friday on the square of the main cathedral in Vilnius. The statues were pulled down one night in 1950 on the eve of a visit by a high-ranking Soviet official, Mikhail Suslov.
- The government decided to boost the share capital of problem-hit Innovation bank to 510 million litas.
- Lietuvos Energija accumulated 300,000 tonnes of heating oil or 138,000 tonnes less than the same period last year.
